pageCache.pageTitle: Ospringe C of E Primary School - Mental health & wellbeing
pageCache.text:
Mental health & wellbeing
At our school, mental health and wellbeing are of the highest importance. In line with our strapline Nurture, Grow, Succeed, we believe that every child needs to feel safe, supported, and valued in order to flourish. We are committed to nurturing each pupil so they are in the right place—emotionally and socially—to grow in their learning and achieve success. Our dedicated staff provide caring, consistent support and work closely with families to identify individual needs. When appropriate, we make referrals to external agencies, such as the school nurse, to ensure that every child receives the right help at the right time. Through this joined-up approach, we strive to create a school community where all pupils can thrive.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ospringe C of E Primary School - Maths
pageCache.text:
Maths
At Ospringe, we use Power Maths to teach mathematics because it helps every child develop a deep and secure understanding of the subject. Power Maths is based on a mastery approach, which means children learn concepts in small, carefully planned steps. This ensures that no one is left behind, while also challenging those who are ready to move forward. Lessons are designed to build confidence, encourage curiosity, and promote problem-solving skills, making maths both enjoyable and meaningful for all learners.
The benefits of Power Maths go beyond learning calculations—it helps children develop important life skills such as logical thinking, perseverance, and teamwork. Through engaging activities, children are encouraged to explain their reasoning, discuss ideas with others, and find different ways to solve problems. This approach not only strengthens their mathematical understanding but also helps them to become confident, independent learners who are ready to tackle challenges both in and out of the classroom.

Ospringe C of E Primary School - Attendance
pageCache.text:
Attendance
To get the best out of school and all it has to offer, children need to come to school every day and be on time.
Ospringe CE Primary Pupil Attendance
Good school attendance is paramount to every child’s success. Our aim at Ospringe CE Primary is for every child to enjoy school, embrace all the opportunities offered and achieve their best potential.
As a parent, ensuring your child’s regular attendance at school is a legal responsibility and permitting absence from school without good reason can be classed as an offence.
What the Government Says…
Government guidelines state that an attendance figure of 90% or less is classed as a ‘persistent absence’. The government identifies a good level of attendance as 95% or more. At Ospringe, we will inform you each term of your child’s attendance rates. We will also notify you if we feel that your child’s attendance needs to be improved.
At Ospringe, we expect children to attend school every day, as long as they are fit and healthy enough to do so.
We understand that there can be tricky times and, as ever, we are always on hand to offer you any support that you feel you need. If there are ever any problems, please do not hesitate to come and see us and let us know how we can help.
What the Numbers Tell Us…
If your child attends school between 95% and 100%, they are on track to achieve their very best and enjoy all that school has to offer.
Just 10 days absence in a year can take your child’s attendance down to 94.7%
Whilst a figure of 90% sounds good, in reality, this means that your child has missed half a day of school every week or a full month of the year. If a child only attended school for 90% of the year, every year, throughout his or her primary school career, this would equate to one whole school year missed in total.
If your child is off school due to illness or an appointment, please contact the school before 8.50am, to explain why they will not be with us
If you have not informed us of your child’s whereabouts by 9.30am, we have to contact you as part of our safeguarding process. If your child is going to be in late after an appointment, we ask that you inform us as to whether your child will need a school dinner.
Attendance is monitored regularly by the local authority. We will inform you if your child’s attendance becomes a cause for concern or falls below 95%
Holiday/Leave of absence from school
The school will not authorise time off for family holidays/events and will issue penalty notices.
Please ask in the office if you require a copy of our Attendance policy. If you need to make an application for leave please contact the school office. Please do not take holiday in term time.
